title: HouseVis: house model
description: Simplified model of a house for HouseVis. Coordinates in meters, x to the east, y to the north, origin freely chosen (e.g. southwest corner of the main building). All rooms are interior areas (structural dimensions without plaster); walls result from the gaps between the rooms. Walls may run in any direction. Limits of the model: the floors stand directly on top of each other in the given order.

^(\\$schema|_.*)$.description: Reference to the schema or a comment; ignored.

version.description: Format version of this file. HouseVis converts older files from version 6 on when it loads them (the Windows app writes the result back and keeps the old file as house.v<n>.json); anything else is refused with a message.

data.description: House-wide datapoints from datapoints.json per role.

outsideBrightness.description: Brightness outside in lux (number), e.g. the brightness sensor of the Loxone weather station; the scene's daylight follows it, so lit rooms and light sources stand out at dusk and night. Without it the scene keeps its daylight look.

outsideTemperature.description: Outside temperature in °C (number), shown large in the weather station's panel. Loxone offers it from the weather station, the weather service and the merged System value; the System value may include further sensors (e.g. a heat pump's shaded one) and is usually the best ambient temperature.

feltTemperature.description: Felt temperature in °C (number), e.g. the Loxone weather service's.

windSpeed.description: Wind speed in km/h (number); the anemometer turns with it, the clouds drift with it.

windDirection.description: Wind direction in degrees (number), where the wind comes from: 0 north, 90 east (meteorological convention, as Loxone delivers it).

windWarning.description: Wind warning (true/false), e.g. the weather station's; the anemometer turns red while it is on.

rain.description: Rain right now (true/false), e.g. the weather station's rain sensor; adds light rain when the weather type says none.

sunshine.description: The sun is shining (true/false); a screen with weather shows the sun only then.

weatherType.description: Weather type of the Loxone weather service (number, codes 1–29 as Loxone documents them, docs/weather.md); a screen with weather shows the sky and precipitation for it.

floors.description: Floors from bottom to top. The height is the floor-to-floor height (including the ceiling).

id.description: Short id, e.g. "ug", "eg", "og".

exteriorWall.description: Thickness of the exterior walls in meters (structural, e.g. 0.365). They lie outside the room polygons: the outer face is the room edge moved outwards by this much, and windows sit in the reveal. Default 0: the facade lies on the room edges.

rooms.description: Rooms as they are named in the home automation. A room may consist of several areas (e.g. bedroom with walk-in closet).

id.description: Stable id that areas, views and data sources refer to.

name.description: Display name on the wall, as short as possible.

data.description: Datapoints from datapoints.json per role. Value types: temperature, targetTemperature, humidity, lightLevel, climateMode and climateOverride number; heating, light and presence true/false; lightColor color.

humidity.description: Relative humidity in percent (number), e.g. the room's Touch (T5) humidity sensor; shown in the temperature label's small line beside the target temperature, rounded to whole percent.

heating.description: Heating active (true/false); shows a flame. Best the room controller's demand (conversion "climateDemand"), since a valve also opens for cooling.

cooling.description: Cooling active (true/false); shows a snowflake. The room controller's demand (conversion "climateDemand").

light.description: Light on (true/false); the room is then shown lit.

lightColor.description: Light color (color); the room then glows in this color. A list mixes the colors of several channels, e.g. all outputs of a light controller: moods set the channels, the master color does not report them back.

lightLevel.description: Brightness of the light in percent (number, 0–100), only for light without brightness in the light color. Without this role the brightness from lightColor applies. Not the master brightness of a light controller: it is only a factor on the active mood.

climateMode.description: The heat controller's active mode (IRoomControllerV2 "activeMode": 0 eco, 1 comfort, 2 building protection); shown as an icon in the temperature label.

climateOverride.description: The heat controller's override reason ("overrideReason"); 2 (window open) and 15 (pause timer) show the room as paused.

spaces.description: Floor areas of the rooms. Each area is a simple polygon of interior dimensions (edges in any direction, no self-crossing). Interior walls result from gaps narrower than 0.7 m between areas.

id.description: Unique id of the area, e.g. the room id; views and wall ids refer to it, so keep it stable.

roomId.description: Room whose values this area shows.

name.description: Plan name of its own if the area belongs to another room (e.g. "Ankleide" to the bedroom). Such areas get no label of their own.

floor.description: Id of the floor.

polygon.description: Corner points [x, y] of the interior area in meters, in order. Edges may run in any direction; the outline must not cross itself.

height.description: Deviating room height in meters; otherwise the floor height applies (for an area with "openTo" the heights of the storeys it passes).

openTo.description: A double-height space ("Luftraum", a two-storey bay or hall): id of the highest storey above its own this area is open through. Those storeys have no floor slab over it and no area of theirs may overlap it; its windows may reach up into them ("top" up to the heights of all these storeys). Written on the lower area, which is the room standing there (e.g. the living room under the Luftraum).

outbuilding.description: Lies outside the main building (e.g. garage) and does not count as a wall neighbor. A building of its own: with "exteriorWall" it has walls (facade from outside, room walls when active), without them it is an open shelter showing only its floor.

exteriorWall.description: Outbuildings only: thickness of their walls in meters, outside the polygon like the house's (the polygon is the inside). Without it the outbuilding has no walls.

level.description: Outbuildings only: their floor relative to the storey's in meters, e.g. -0.32 for a garage lower than the house. "height" then counts from this floor; openings keep counting from the storey's.

facadeColor.description: Color of the exterior wall when the area is seen from outside in a view (default white).

openings.description: Windows and doors in the walls: exterior ones, and interior doors, passages and glass partitions between two rooms (on an interior edge, the room across the wall found by itself).

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "kueche-west-1"; datapoints, views and the editor refer to it.

tilted.description: Tilted (true/false), only for contacts that distinguish it.

position.description: Degree of opening 0 (closed) to 1 (fully open), e.g. for motorized windows.

start.description: One end of the opening in the floor plan, on the inner face of its wall, i.e. on an edge of the room polygon (5 mm tolerance). The room and the outward direction follow from that edge; on an interior wall either room's face, the room across the wall gap follows too. In a dormer's front: on its inner face or on the outer face as "front" gives it; the room behind it and the dormer's facing follow.

end.description: The other end, on the same edge. The order of start and end does not matter.

sill.description: Bottom edge above the floor of the storey in meters. Negative only in an outbuilding whose floor lies lower (e.g. a garage at −0.32: its gates start there).

top.description: Top edge above the floor of the storey in meters.

operation.description: Type: "none" a door without a leaf (a passage between rooms, only the hole through the wall); "turn" side-hung sash (opens inwards, windows 30°, doors 90°), "slide" sliding sash (e.g. lift-and-slide door), "top-hung" hinged at the top (opens outwards at the bottom), "overhead" garage gate opening upwards into the room (up-and-over or sectional; one leaf, "position" is the share of the height that is clear), "fixed" fixed glazing. Default "turn".

side.description: Seen from inside: hinge side for "turn", direction in which a "slide" sash opens. Default "left".

leaves.description: Number of sashes (default 1). With 2 and "turn" both sashes open towards the middle (hinges on the outside); with 2 and "slide" one sash slides in front of the other, towards "side".

fixedBelow.description: Height of a fixed, non-opening lower part in meters from the bottom edge (e.g. balustrade glazing).

sidelight.description: Fixed glazed side panel next to the sash, e.g. at a front door. The width counts towards the opening.

color.description: A door's leaf color; a window's frame color (frame, sash frames, fixed parts), e.g. "#f2f2f0" for white frames. Default: dark brown-grey leaves, grey frames.

glass.description: Doors only: a glazed leaf, drawn like a window pane (a glass door, e.g. a sauna's or a patio door's).

frame.description: false: frameless glass, held by fittings only (a sauna's glass front and door, a glass partition); no frame drawn. Default true.

dormers.description: Dormers (Gauben), each standing on one slope of a roof part and written by its front, as plans dimension it. It faces down the slope, its front along the slope's eave; its cheeks reach back to where its eave (gable) or its roof (shed) meets the slope. The host roof is cut away under it, and the rooms below get its ceiling. Windows in its front are ordinary openings.

id.description: Unique among roof parts and dormers, e.g. "gaube-nord".

roof.description: Id of the roof part from "roofs" it stands on; its heights refer to that part's floor.

kind.description: "shed": one slope falling towards the front (Schleppgaube); "gable": two slopes with a gable over the front (Giebelgaube).

front.description: The outer face of the front wall in the floor plan: its two ends, in either order.

eaveHeight.description: Height above the floor, in meters, of the front wall's top (shed) or of the cheeks' top (gable), at the outer face.

pitch.description: Pitch of the dormer's roof in degrees; a shed dormer's must be less than the slope it stands on.

overhang.description: How far its roof reaches beyond the front and beyond the cheeks, in meters: one value, or { "front": 0.3, "sides": 0.15 }. Default 0.

color.description: Color of its roof covering; default the roof part's.

wallColor.description: Color of its front and cheeks seen from outside, e.g. "#5a5e63" for slate or zinc cladding; default the facade's.

pvArrays.description: PV arrays: each a rectangle of panels lying in one slope of a roof part, placed like a roof window (the slope under "center" decides); drawn flat on the slope, cut away with the roof. An indicator at an array ("pvArray") shows what it produces.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "pv-south"; an indicator's "pvArray" refers to it.

roof.description: Id of the roof part from "roofs".

center.description: Center of the array in the floor plan.

width.description: Width along the eave (horizontal on the slope) in meters.

depth.description: Extent across the eave, measured in the floor plan (not along the slope), in meters.

roofWindows.description: Roof windows. Each lies in one slope of a roof part; the slope under "center" decides.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "bad-roof-west"; datapoints, views and the editor refer to it.

roof.description: Id of the roof part from "roofs".

center.description: Center of the window in the floor plan.

width.description: Width along the eave (horizontal on the slope) in meters.

depth.description: Extent across the eave, measured in the floor plan (not along the slope), in meters.

data.description: Datapoints from datapoints.json per role. An open roof window flips outwards 20° at the bottom.

position.description: Degree of opening 0 (closed) to 1 (fully open), e.g. for motorized roof windows.

shades.description: Shades; their "from"/"to" are meters along the width from the left edge, seen from outside looking up the slope.

roofs.description: Roof as a list of parts, each as plans dimension it: the wall line it sits on ("outline"), how far it reaches beyond ("overhang"), and its slopes by their height at the wall line. Each slope is a plane through its side of the outline; within a part the surface is the lowest of them, cut off at the outline plus the overhangs (a "polygon" part: the lowest of those whose edge reaches the point). Where parts overlap, the higher one counts (e.g. a wing running into the main roof forms valleys). Rooms on a part's floor end below its slopes.

oneOf.description: Gable roof: two slopes on the sides along the ridge, vertical gable walls at both ends. With "ridgeHeight" both slopes have the same pitch; with different eave heights or overhangs the ridge moves accordingly.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

ridge.description: Direction of the ridge (before rotation); the slopes lie on the two sides along it (east-west: south and north).

oneOf.description: Half-hip roof (Krüppelwalm): a gable roof whose gable walls end below the ridge in a small hip. The two slopes as for "gable"; at each gable end a hip slope starting at "hipEaveHeight" on the gable's wall line, rising at "hipPitch". Per side (the gable ends: west and east for an east-west ridge) for different ends, or for a half-hip at one end only.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

ridge.description: Direction of the ridge (before rotation); the slopes lie on the two sides along it, the half-hips at its ends.

hipEaveHeight.description: Where the half-hip starts: its height above the floor at the gable's wall line (the top of the gable wall, sections give it as the hip's eave), between the eaves and the ridge. One value for both ends, or per gable side; a gable side without one stays a full gable.

hipPitch.description: Pitch of the half-hip in degrees (usually steeper than the slopes), one value or per gable side, for the same sides as "hipEaveHeight".

oneOf.description: Hip roof: a slope on every side. With "ridgeHeight" all four have the same pitch and the ridge is shorter than the outline by its width.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

ridge.description: Direction of the ridge (before rotation); "ridgeHeight" is reached by the slopes across it.

oneOf.description: Shed roof: one slope down towards side "low".

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

low.description: Side of the outline (before rotation) towards which the roof slopes down.

eaveHeight.description: Height at the low side's wall line above the floor, in meters.

ridgeHeight.description: Height at the high side's wall line above the floor, in meters; or "pitch" instead.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

height.description: Height above the floor in meters.

oneOf.description: Roof with a polygon outline (an L, T or U, a main roof with a cross gable, a wrap-around canopy): every edge of the outline carries a slope or ends in a gable wall. Each slope rises inwards from its edge; at an outside corner two slopes meet in a hip, at an inside corner in a valley. Use the rectangle kinds where they fit.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "main"; roof windows, views and the editor refer to it.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to; the rooms of that floor end below the roof.

outline.description: The wall line under the roof, corner by corner in either direction: the outer faces of the walls it sits on (Außenkante); a roof over no walls (carport, canopy) its own edges without overhang. Edge i runs from corner i to the next (the last back to the first).

eaveHeight.description: Height of the slopes at the wall line, above the floor; an edge may give its own.

pitch.description: Pitch of the slopes in degrees; an edge may give its own. 0 on every edge: a flat roof at "eaveHeight".

overhang.description: How far the roof reaches beyond every edge, in meters (default 0); an edge may give its own.

edges.description: One entry per edge of "outline", in the same order (edge i from corner i to the next): "slope", "gable" (a vertical gable wall closes the roof there), or an object giving that edge its own values.

eaveHeight.description: This slope's height at the wall line.

overhang.description: How far the roof reaches beyond this edge (a gable's verge).

ground.description: Terrain around the house. Shown as a translucent surface so one can see which floors lie in the ground.

floor.description: Floor whose level "level", "heights" and the heights of pits and platforms refer to.

level.description: Height of a flat terrain relative to that floor in meters, e.g. -0.3. Give either this or "heights".

heights.description: Spot heights of a sloped terrain, as a site plan gives them: [x, y, level] with the level relative to the floor of "floor" (not above sea level). The terrain runs linearly between them (triangles between neighbouring points); two points or points on one line give a slope along that line, level across it; outside the points the slope continues. Give either this or "level".

outline.description: Where the terrain ends: its outline in plan coordinates, at least 3 corners in order, at any angle (a plot ending at a street that does not run north-south). The terrain is exactly this outline: nothing is derived from the house, the garage or the areas, so the model decides where the plot ends (e.g. at the street). The house and its outbuildings lie inside it; parts of areas outside it are cut off.

pits.description: Excavated areas, e.g. in front of basement windows: vertical walls down to "bottom". Sides along the house stay open.

polygon.description: The footprint at any angle, corners in plan coordinates (docs/polygon-footprints.md); instead of x0/x1/y0/y1, which give a rectangle.

bottom.description: Bottom relative to the floor of ground.floor, in meters.

railing.description: Railing along the free top edges.

tags.description: Tags of the pit in addition to the terrain's ("ground", "outside"), e.g. "Lichtschacht": a view that hides one leaves the pit out and the terrain closes over it. A switch on a page hides its walls, stairs and railing, but leaves its opening in the terrain.

stairs.description: Stairs in the pit, only hinted: the steps descend towards side "down" down to "bottom".

down.description: Direction in which the stairs lead down.

landing.description: Length of the landing at the bottom end in meters.

areas.description: Areas in the terrain with their own color, e.g. terrace, gravel strip or paving; with "level" a flat platform. Nothing is drawn below the house. Where areas overlap, the last one listed wins.

polygon.description: The footprint at any angle, corners in plan coordinates (docs/polygon-footprints.md); instead of x0/x1/y0/y1, which give a rectangle.

level.description: Makes the area a platform lying flat at this level (relative to the floor of ground.floor), e.g. a terrace or a drive cut into a slope; where the terrain round it lies higher or lower, an edge (retaining wall, embankment) is drawn. Without it the area follows the terrain.

structures.description: Simple boxes outside the house, e.g. steps, landing, pillars or the lintel above the entrance. Floor-plan coordinates as for the rooms, heights relative to the floor of "floor".

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "pfeiler-eingang"; views refer to it ("structures" in views/<id>.json) to make the part transparent or hide it.

name.description: For orientation only; the editor shows it to name the part.

polygon.description: The footprint at any angle, corners in plan coordinates (docs/polygon-footprints.md); instead of x0/x1/y0/y1, which give a rectangle.

bottom.description: Bottom edge relative to the floor in meters.

top.description: Top edge relative to the floor in meters.

transparent.description: Only hinted (like a cut-open wall), e.g. when the part lies in front of a room one looks into.

pavilions.description: Light glass extensions such as a conservatory, hinted only by their outer edges. With "roomId" they show values of a room from rooms (e.g. light).

roomId.description: Room from rooms whose values (light) the extension shows.

floor.description: Floor whose level the heights refer to.

polygon.description: The footprint at any angle, corners in plan coordinates (docs/polygon-footprints.md); instead of x0/x1/y0/y1, which give a rectangle.

top.description: Top edge at the house in meters.

lowTop.description: Top edge at the low side in meters.

low.description: Side towards which the roof slopes down (away from the house).

weatherStation.description: The weather station on or by the house, drawn as a cup anemometer on a short mast where it really stands (docs/weather.md); the weather panel (temperature, felt temperature, wind, humidity from "data") hangs at it. The mast reaches down to the roof or terrain below. Implied tags "weatherStation" and "outside", plus "roof" when it stands on a roof, so the view's tag buttons can show or hide it.

floor.description: Storey its height refers to; for a station on a roof the storey the roof part belongs to.

position.description: Where the mast stands, in floor-plan coordinates.

height.description: Height of the cups above the storey's floor, in meters; above the roof or terrain at that point.

lights.description: Light sources besides the room light (docs/lights.md): lanterns along a walkway, wall lights on the facade, lit furniture inside (pendant over the dining table, lit cupboards). Each shows its own light, or its room's without "data". Floor-plan coordinates as for the rooms. The house-model skill places them; they are not edited by hand in the app.

oneOf.description: Hangs from the ceiling over a point and shines down, e.g. over the dining table: a bell-shaped shade, or a slim tube ("shape").

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "esstisch" or "weg-1".

floor.description: Storey the light belongs to; its heights are above that storey's floor, like everywhere in house.json.

room.description: Room from rooms whose light it follows when it has no "data". Default: the room of the area it lies in; give it only where the point cannot tell.

data.description: Datapoints from datapoints.json per role, as for rooms: light true/false, lightColor color (a list mixes several channels), lightLevel number 0–100. Without any the light follows its room's light. Typically one output (LCx, subcontrol AIx, state "color") of a light controller, or a switch.

lightColor.description: Light color (color); a list mixes the colors of several channels.

lightLevel.description: Brightness in percent (number, 0–100), only for a light without brightness in its color, e.g. a dimmer.

color.description: Color of the lamp body while it is off; default per kind.

size.description: Main dimension of the lamp body in meters (shade diameter, lantern head, width of a wall light); default per kind. Not for strips: their length is from–to.

range.description: How far the light reaches, in meters; default per kind.

beamAngle.description: Opening angle of the light cone in degrees, for lights shining in one direction; default per kind.

position.description: Point in the floor plan under the lamp.

height.description: Lower edge of the lamp above the floor, in meters (e.g. 1.5 over a table).

shape.description: bell (default): an open shade, wide light, the shade glowing when lit. tube: a slim closed cylinder ("size" its diameter, default 0.06; "length"), light only from its lower end in a narrow beam (default 40°), only that end glowing.

length.description: Only with "shape": "tube": length of the tube in meters; default 0.3. Its top (height + length) lies below the ceiling.

oneOf.description: Recessed in the ceiling, shines down.

beamAngle.description: Opening angle of the light cone in degrees, for lights shining in one direction; default per kind.

position.description: Point on the inner face of the wall, i.e. on an edge of a room polygon, like the ends of an opening; also for a light on the facade ("side": "outside").

side.description: Face of the wall it hangs on: inside the room, or outside on the facade (only on an exterior wall).

height.description: Center of the light above the floor, in meters.

beam.description: Where it shines along the wall; default down.

oneOf.description: A line of light, e.g. under a wall cupboard, in a shelf or a cove: either placed by "floor", "from", "to" and "height", or along an edge of a piece of furniture ("on"), which gives it all of these.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. "esstisch" or "weg-1".

floor.description: Storey the light belongs to; its heights are above that storey's floor, like everywhere in house.json.

room.description: Room from rooms whose light it follows when it has no "data". Default: the room of the area it lies in; give it only where the point cannot tell.

data.description: Datapoints from datapoints.json per role, as for rooms: light true/false, lightColor color (a list mixes several channels), lightLevel number 0–100. Without any the light follows its room's light. Typically one output (LCx, subcontrol AIx, state "color") of a light controller, or a switch.

lightColor.description: Light color (color); a list mixes the colors of several channels.

lightLevel.description: Brightness in percent (number, 0–100), only for a light without brightness in its color, e.g. a dimmer.

color.description: Color of the lamp body while it is off; default per kind.

size.description: Main dimension of the lamp body in meters (shade diameter, lantern head, width of a wall light); default per kind. Not for strips: their length is from–to.

range.description: How far the light reaches, in meters; default per kind.

beamAngle.description: Opening angle of the light cone in degrees, for lights shining in one direction; default per kind.

from.description: One end in the floor plan.

to.description: The other end in the floor plan.

height.description: Height above the floor, in meters (a strip: of its "from" end).

on.description: Along an edge of a piece of furniture, its whole length; the strip moves with the piece and goes with its tags. Instead of "floor", "from", "to", "height" and "toHeight".

edge.description: Where two faces meet, named from the piece's front, left and right as seen standing in front of it. On a bottom edge the light falls down (under a cupboard), on a top edge it rises (a cove on top), on an upright edge it spreads outwards.

toHeight.description: Only strips: height of the "to" end above the floor, for a strip that rises (under a sloped ceiling, along stairs) or stands upright ("from" and "to" the same point). Default: "height", a level strip.

furniture.description: Furniture as simple boxes (docs/lights.md): lines with a faint fill, shown with its room; its edges can carry light strips. Either against a wall ("from", "to": its back edge, "depth"), which also fits a slanted wall, or along the plan axes ("x0"…"y1" and "front"). Implied tags "furniture", the tags of the area it stands in, and "outside" outside the building.

name.description: Name as the user calls it, e.g. "Oberschrank".

floor.description: Storey it stands on; its heights are above that storey's floor.

room.description: Room it belongs to: it shows when a view opens that room. Default: the room of the area its middle lies in; give it only where the footprint cannot tell.

bottom.description: Bottom edge above the floor in meters (0 for a standing piece, e.g. 1.45 for a wall cupboard).

top.description: Top edge above the floor in meters.

color.description: Color of its lines and faint fill; default a light grey.

opacity.description: How strongly its faces are filled: 0 lines only, 1 solid; default faint (0.25).

from.description: Left end of its back edge, seen standing in front of it (plan point, e.g. on the wall it stands against).

to.description: Right end of its back edge, seen from the front.

depth.description: From the back edge towards the front, in meters.

name.description: Name as the user calls it, e.g. "Oberschrank".

floor.description: Storey it stands on; its heights are above that storey's floor.

room.description: Room it belongs to: it shows when a view opens that room. Default: the room of the area its middle lies in; give it only where the footprint cannot tell.

bottom.description: Bottom edge above the floor in meters (0 for a standing piece, e.g. 1.45 for a wall cupboard).

top.description: Top edge above the floor in meters.

color.description: Color of its lines and faint fill; default a light grey.

opacity.description: How strongly its faces are filled: 0 lines only, 1 solid; default faint (0.25).

front.description: The side its front faces; edges are named from it (left and right as seen standing in front).

indicators.description: Indicators that appear depending on the state of datapoints, e.g. notes while music is playing. One thing is one indicator, its states are rules: they are checked in order and the first matching one applies (a rule without "when" always matches, e.g. "no mail" last); if none matches, the indicator is hidden. The icon comes from the kind (global.json), which a rule may change for its state.

room.description: Room in whose row of indicators it appears (each view places the row, "labels" in the view file; default just below the ceiling).

position.description: A point of its own instead of a room's row, for an indicator that belongs to a place (the mailbox by the front door): "height" is the icon's middle above the storey's floor (default 1.5). It shows with the room of the area the point lies in, or as "outside".

pvArray.description: Id of a PV array from "pvArrays": the icon floats above the array's centre, instead of a room's row or a "position", for what that array produces (a "value" with its power). It shows while the view draws the array's roof part and goes with that part's tags ("roof").

tags.description: Only with "position" or "pvArray": tags of its own besides those of the area it lies in (at a PV array: those of the array's roof part).

value.description: Shows a datapoint's value beside the icon (a pool's temperature, a room's humidity), while a rule shows the indicator ("rules": [{}] always). A kind without an icon (global.json) shows the value alone. Written in the datapoint's "format" (Loxone's, e.g. "%.1f°"), else with its "unit".

datapoint.description: Datapoint from datapoints.json, a number or a text.

kind.description: Different kind (and so icon) for this state, e.g. "music-paused".

stairs.description: Stairs between storeys (docs/stairs.md), written by their walking line as a plan draws it. Where a stair climbs into the storey above, it cuts the opening into that storey's slab and floors.

floor.description: The storey the stair starts on.

to.description: The storey it arrives on; default the next one up.

line.description: The walking line (Lauflinie) in the middle of the stair, in plan coordinates: from the front edge of the first step to the edge of the upper floor, with a corner wherever the stair turns (two points straight, three an L, four a U). Every corner turns by 90°.

width.description: Width of the stair in metres, e.g. 1.0.

rises.description: Number of rises (Steigungen) from floor to floor, as a plan prints it ("16 St. 17,8/27": 16).

turns.description: One per corner of the line: "landing" (a square landing, the default) or "winders" (the corner's steps fanned, a gewendelte stair).

color.description: Colour of the steps; default a light stone grey.

tags.description: Tags in addition to "stairs" and those of the area it starts in.

railings.description: Railings (docs/railings.md): along a plan line on a storey (gallery edge, balcony, roof terrace) or along a stair's side. A line railing standing in an interior wall's gap opens that wall along it; exterior walls are never opened.

floor.description: The storey a line railing stands on.

line.description: Its course in plan coordinates, at any angle. On a gallery's edge, in the wall gap towards the open space (at most 0.5 m off the wall), where it opens the wall.

stair.description: Instead of floor and line: the stair whose side it follows.

side.description: The stair's side, seen walking up.

kind.description: glass: panes with a top rail; bars: handrail, bottom rail and upright bars; solid: a closed parapet.

height.description: Its top above its foot (default 1.0), or above the stair's nosings (default 0.9).

base.description: A line railing's foot above its storey's floor, default 0 (e.g. a balcony slab's top).

color.description: Colour of the frame or the parapet.

objects.description: Objects in the house (planned extension), e.g. a floor lamp that looks different when switched on. Either a 3D model from config/models/ or a simple basic shape. Variants are checked in order and the first matching one applies.

rotation.description: Rotation about the vertical axis in degrees.

shape.description: Basic shape if no model is given.

glow.description: Self-illumination, e.g. for a lamp that is switched on.

outline.description: The wall line under a roof part, before "rotation": the outer faces of the walls it sits on (Außenkante), as the plans dimension them. For a roof over no walls (carport, canopy) its own edges.

overhang.description: How far the roof reaches beyond the outline, in meters (eave and verge overhang): one value for every side, or per side (before rotation), e.g. { "south": 0.8, "east": 0.4, "west": 0.4 }; missing sides 0. Default 0.

rotation.description: Degrees counterclockwise around the center of the outline, for houses not aligned with the axes. Default 0.

roofColor.description: Color of the roof covering seen from outside, e.g. "#3a3d40" for anthracite tiles. The seams are drawn a little darker. Default dark red.

eaveHeight.description: Height above the floor, in meters, where a slope meets the outline: at the outer face of the wall (sections give it there, or the knee wall plus the rafter seat). One value for every slope, or per sloped side, e.g. { "south": 1.2, "north": 2.0 }.

ridgeHeight.description: Height of the ridge above the floor, in meters: every slope gets the same pitch, the one at which the slopes across the ridge meet at this height. Give it or "pitch".

pitch.description: Pitch in degrees (DN), one value for every slope or per sloped side; instead of "ridgeHeight", e.g. for slopes of different pitch.

tags.description: Tags of the element in addition to those its kind implies, so a view can leave groups of elements out ("hide" in views/<id>.json). Implied: roof parts "roof" (one that covers only outbuildings also gets their tags, so a "Garage" tag on the garage area reaches its roof); structures "structure"; pavilions "pavilion" and "outside"; outbuildings "outbuilding" (without walls of their own also "outside"); outdoor areas (height 0) "outside"; the terrain and its pits "ground" and "outside"; lights "light", the tags of the area they lie in, and "outside" when outside the building (no area, an outdoor area, or a facade). Add "outside" to what stands apart from the building (a garden wall, freestanding steps) and names of your own for groups, as you call them (e.g. "Garage" on the garage's area, roof part and pillars). An element can carry several tags.

datapointRef.description: Id of a datapoint from datapoints.json.

indicatorKind.description: What an indicator shows, e.g. "music"; global.json assigns each kind its icon ("heating" and "cooling" are the rooms' own).

height.description: Height above the floor of the storey (default 0).

condition.description: Condition on datapoints. Either a comparison with "datapoint" and exactly one of equals, notEquals, above, below, isTrue, isFalse, or a combination with "all" (all) or "any" (at least one).

shades.description: Shading in front of the opening, outside. Usually one; several if e.g. a two-part door has a curtain per part.

kind.description: "roller" roller blind or shutter (Loxone animation 1), "blind" venetian blind with slats (animation 0).

from.description: Start, if the shading covers only part of the opening: for wall openings meters from "start", for roof windows meters along the width from the left edge seen from outside looking up the slope.

position.description: Closed 0 (open, up) to 1 (fully down); for Loxone "position" on the Jalousie control.

slats.description: Slat angle 0 (horizontal, open) to 1 (closed); for Loxone "shadePosition".
